title: QUANTITY OF HUON PINE DOOR PAN...
reason: Seven old timber cupboard doors and panels described as Huon pine, a valued Tasmanian timber; species not confirmed by the photos (one door looks like common pine).
findings: Seven timber cupboard door and panel pieces: four arched-panel cupboard doors (two honey-gold doors hinged together, one more honey-gold door, and one paler stripped door with hinges on its right edge) with white porcelain knobs and brass butt hinges, plus three loose flat panels with moulded arched or rectangular panels (drawer or door fronts) in a deeper golden-orange finish. The timber is a golden-yellow softwood with fine, fairly straight grain, compatible with the title's Huon pine on the loose panels and the left doors, but one door shows a large dark knot with a reddish ring that looks more like common pine, so the species is not confirmed by the photos. No maker's marks or stamps visible; only a paper tag on one door. Looks like salvage from an old built-in cupboard.
condition: Doors show surface wear and an old finish; the pale right-hand door has lost its finish and has orange-brown stains; brass butt hinges still fitted to some doors; loose panels have a few small dark spots (nail holes or pin knots); no splits or breaks visible in the photo; loose panels have no knobs or hinges.
rescore_note: Everything turns on species: genuine Huon pine would give the seven pieces real timber value (saved research, seen 2026-10-01: huonpine.com.au asking A$205 for a cracked 1840 x 430 x 25 mm slab, https://huonpine.com.au/product/huon-slab-256-1840mm-430mm-25mm/), but the photos show honey pine with a dark knot and stripped stains that look as much like common pine; blended, on the line between the $30-80 and $80-200 bands.
